subject: Demo recap + proposed POC playbook — Solaris Systems
messages:
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@solaris.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-03T15:22:00-07:00
Subject: Demo recap + proposed POC playbook — Solaris Systems

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciated the thoughtful questions from you and Ken. Quick recap from our side and a concrete proposal for a short POC so your team can validate latency, accuracy, and integration workstreams without a heavy lift.

TL;DR: attached is a 1-page playbook + checklist (Solaris-POC-Playbook-v1.pdf / poc-checklist.xlsx). Proposed scope:
- Objective: validate Redwood inference for intent extraction and multi-turn slot filling inside Solaris' customer support flow
- Success criteria (pass if ALL met):
  - Intent classification F1 >= 0.88 on your sampled dataset
  - End-to-end median latency (p50) < 300ms for 512-token requests in staging
  - End-to-end demo with your QA team and no manual preprocessing required beyond current pipelines
- Duration: 3 weeks (kickoff -> baseline eval -> two tuning sprints -> final run + handoff)
- Owners: Redwood SE lead: Lukas Meyer; Solutions Eng: Ben Carter; CSM: Marissa Cole; Solaris: Elena Ruiz (product), Ken Wu (CTO), Priya Shah (ML)

Proposed kickoff: Tue 2026-09-08 10:00 PT (we can shift if needed). Can you confirm stakeholders and any mandatory security/compliance constraints we should bake into the plan (VPN, SAS tokens, SOC2 evidence review window)?

Attachments: [Attachment: Solaris-POC-Playbook-v1.pdf (application/pdf) - 184KB], [Attachment: poc-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet) - 24KB]

Next steps (if yes):
1) Confirm kickoff time and point-of-contact for data access
2) Redwood provides an onboarding checklist and short S3 transfer guide
3) We ship a baseline eval within 7 business days of data receipt

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lukas_meyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Lukas — thanks for the clear follow-up and the playbook. We are keen to move forward. A few quick clarifications from our side before we lock the kickoff: 

1) Success criteria tweaks:
   - Intent F1: target >= 0.90 if possible (we can be flexible but would like to see improvement thresholds vs baseline)
   - Latency: p50 < 300ms is fine; p95 < 700ms would be ideal for production readiness

2) Data & security:
   - We prefer S3 presigned upload to our sandbox bucket. We cannot provide direct VPN access to vendor infra.
   - We will need SOC2 Type II evidence and a short list of network/IPs for allowlisting prior to any inbound data transfers.

3) Stakeholders:
   - Ken (CTO) will attend kickoff for the first 30 minutes. Priya (Head of ML) will own dataset prep and evaluation priorities. I will own product acceptance.

Can you confirm that presigned S3 uploads + staging endpoints will work, and whether Redwood can provide SOC2 summary and an IP allowlist by EOD Monday?

If yes, we can confirm Tue 2026-09-08 10:00 PT for kickoff.

Elena Ruiz
Director of Product | Solaris Systems
elena@solaris.ai | +1 (650) 555-7789

Elena / team — jumping in with the technical checklist and a small adjustment to timeline based on integration work.

Notes:
- Presigned S3 uploads are ideal — we can provide a short runbook for schema expectations and a sample ingestion script.
- For the latency target, we'll use a staging cluster close to your region (us-west) and run tests with sequence profiles you shared. Quantized model variants (8-bit) will likely be the best tradeoff for latency without large quality loss; we'll include that in the baseline.
- Data volume: please aim for 1,000 to 5,000 representative conversational threads (anonymized) for the first run; we'll surface per-intent confusion matrices and suggested prompt/label fixes.
- Compliance: SOC2 summary we can attach; IP allowlist will be a small set of egress endpoints (I will circulate these separately).

Adjusted timeline (recommended):
Week 0 (kickoff + data transfer window)
Week 1 (baseline run & initial tuning)
Week 2 (tuning sprint + integration checks)
Week 3 (final run, QA session & acceptance)

If Solaris prefers a condensed 2-week sprint we can compress milestones but risk less tuning iterations — flagging for visibility.

Attachment: [Attachment: integration-wireframe.png (image/png) - 32KB] — a simple flow of where the staged endpoint will sit relative to your QA harness.

I can prepare the ingestion script and a small sample pipeline Monday AM after we have the presigned bucket details.

—Ben
